        From 4cded138238db6b3ba8bf208fa3b39f200f7067d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Masahiro Ide <imasahiro9@gmail.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Apr 2014 16:36:44 +0900

---
 java/src/libbun/parser/ast/ZNode.java | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/java/src/libbun/parser/ast/ZNode.java b/java/src/libbun/parser/ast/ZNode.java
index 9b71d71..54c0c73 100644
--- a/java/src/libbun/parser/ast/ZNode.java
+++ b/java/src/libbun/parser/ast/ZNode.java
@@ -51,7 +51,7 @@ public abstract class ZNode {
 
 	public ZNode(ZNode ParentNode, ZToken SourceToken, int Size) {
 		assert(this != ParentNode);
-		ParentNode.SetChild(this, ZNode._EnforcedParent);
+		this.ParentNode = ParentNode;
 		this.SourceToken = SourceToken;
 		if(Size > 0) {
 			this.AST = LibZen._NewNodeArray(Size);
--

Root cause: The bug was introduced due to modifying the parent-child relationship management within the `ZNode` class. Instead of correctly assigning the current node's parent to the `this.ParentNode` field, the previous code mistakenly called the method `SetChild` on the `ParentNode`, which likely invalidated the tree structure. By changing it back to properly set `this.ParentNode`, the integrity of the node hierarchy is restored, fixing the relationship issue between the nodes.

Root cause:
The bug was introduced due to modifying the parent-child relationship management within the `ZNode` class. Instead of correctly assigning the current node's parent to the `this.ParentNode` field, the previous code mistakenly called the method `SetChild` on the `ParentNode`, which likely invalidated the tree structure. By changing it back to properly set `this.ParentNode`, the integrity of the node hierarchy is restored, fixing the relationship issue between the nodes.
